correctness.rationale: The signed presentation is equivalent to representing H=(sigma(n)-2n)/2 by distinct proper nontrivial divisors. For odd abundant square a with C=sigma(a), Delta=C-2a=2q+1, an odd coprime nonsquare m with E=C(sigma(m)-m)<m has H=qm+(m+E)/2, strictly between qm+E and (q+1)m. Every eligible subset sum is Bm+R with integer B>=0 and 0<=R<=E, hence misses H. For fixed P=product of primes <=4C, the identity sum_{(m,P)=1,m<=X}(sigma(m)/m-1) = sum_{d>1,(d,P)=1} #(h<=X/d,(h,P)=1)/d yields <=rho_P X/(4C)+o(X), because d>4C and sum_{d>4C}1/d²<=1/(4C). Markov gives at least (3/4)rho_P X+o(X) admissible rough cofactors; deleting squares is O(sqrt X), and n=am rescales density by 1/a. The sigma(11025)=22971 arithmetic and strict interval were separately checked; three admissible prime/composite cofactors, exact divisor-convolution X=300, and source Git tree were independently verified. Infinite proof is analytical, not finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The natural question of positive-density odd nonsquare signed-divisor exceptions is valuable, but the previously published October 13 theorem already answers it at equal generality, and quantitatively more strongly for all odd abundant squares. The submitted divisor-sum interval and Markov rough-cofactor argument are a correct alternative derivation using standard techniques; after removing the covered statement, no new motivated invariant, classification, cutoff, or substantive mathematical fact remains. Correctness and reproducibility do not make this redundant derivation a separate valuable scientific finding.
